a, Datasets were curated and compiled as described in Fig. 1a. The remaining pipeline was run separately and in parallel for mouse and human data. All computation was performed in R. Schematic created in BioRender; Wang, H. https://biorender.com/w8x4pii (2026). b, Quality control metrics included ensuring that the number of unique genes per cell (nFeature_RNA) was > 200 and the fraction of mitochondrial reads was <20%. Cells with nFeature_RNA ≥ 95th percentile were also removed as a precaution against doublets. c, Data were then converted into an optimized read/write disk space using BPCells. d, To further streamline computation, all data were then sketched into representative 1,000-cell subsets on a per-study basis. e, The resulting data (12.8 M cells for human or 2.5 M cells for mouse) were then integrated on a per-study basis using three independent approaches (Harmony, scVI, FastMNN), resulting in three distinct clusterings and uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) embeddings. f, Each of the three objects from e were annotated independently in a semi-supervised fashion using canonical markers in conjunction with the automated classification toolkits SingleR and scATOMIC, resulting in seven coarse cell type designations for each of the three distinct objects. g, For each of the six TME cell types (epithelial cells are excluded moving forward), separate and parallel computational pipelines were followed. This begins with pooling all cells designated as a given cell type (e.g., fibroblasts) by any of the three integration approaches, and creating a common object. h, Each cell type-specific object undergoes re-integration using study-specific batch keys, followed by normalization, scaling, principal component analysis (PCA), UMAP, clustering, and re-annotation to assess purity. Improperly classified cells are then removed, and this process of recursive cleaning is repeated until all cells are found to be of the correct cell type. i, Once all cells are found to be correctly classified, the final atlas for that cell type is annotated and final subpopulations are determined. j, As described above, the process from g to i is repeated→ separately for each of the primary six TME cell types in this atlas.

a, Uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) embeddings of 1,000 sketched cells per study integrated using Harmony, scVI, and FastMNN integration techniques. b, UMAP projections of sketched results from each integration approach onto all 12.8 million single cells in the human atlas. Cells are grouped into seven main cell type clusters. c, Dot plots indicating expression levels of characteristic markers for each of the seven cell types. d, Venn diagrams showing overlap in cell annotations among the three integration approaches and the final atlas. e, Ratios of the number of cells in the intersection versus union of Venn diagrams for each cell type in d. Notably, applying the intersection excludes many cells that may be desirable to include in the final atlas. f, Ratio of cells for each type that are included the final atlas compared to those that would have been arrived at by using the intersection of the three integration approaches. Ratios greater than one indicate the presence of cells in our final atlas that would otherwise have been excluded using an intersectional approach. Illustration of the human created in BioRender; Wang, H. https://biorender.com/q41gtvr (2026).

It has been revealed that top-left, UMAP projection based on inferred CNV profiles, where individual cells are colored by their global CNV score. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Freddie Cotton | 20 Nov 2026 21:07, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:15.
  • Marseille welcome Le Mans to the Stade Velodrome on Sunday evening for round 11 of the 2026-27 Ligue 1 campaign.
  • In their previous league outing, Les Olympiens claimed a commendable 2-1 victory over Lens at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis, while Les Manceaux scored late against Monaco on home soil to salvage a point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Freddie Cotton | 20 Nov 2026 21:07, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:15.

Marseille welcome Le Mans to the Stade Velodrome on Sunday evening for round 11 of the 2026-27 Ligue 1 campaign.

In their previous league outing, Les Olympiens claimed a commendable 2-1 victory over Lens at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis, while Les Manceaux scored late against Monaco on home soil to salvage a point.

Following a dismal start to the current league campaign, losing five of their opening six matches to leave them languishing inside the relegation zone and just one point off the foot of the table at the end of September, Marseille will be delighted with how they have bounced back in recent weeks.

Since their narrow 2-1 loss to back-to-back European champions Paris Saint-Germain on September 20, Les Olympiens have been an unstoppable force, winning each of their previous five domestic matches to rise to fourth in the Ligue 1 table and sit just five points off Les Parisiens at the summit.

The biggest strength of Bruno Genesio’s side has undoubtedly been their free flowing attack, as after 10 league games, Marseille have netted an impressive 22 goals, a tally that cannot be bettered by any other side in the division.

However, Les Olympiens will undoubtedly be disappointed with their performances in the UEFA Europa League, as after four league phase fixtures they have picked up just three points and right now reside outside of the tournament’s progression places to the knockout stage.

Having gone unbeaten in each of their previous six encounters with Le Mans, including a 2-1 victory in their most recent meeting at the Stade Velodrome in January 2010, Marseille will be confident that they can continue their fine league form this weekend though and mount a charge towards PSG in top spot.

According to recent reports, after ending their 16-year wait for promotion to France’s top tier at the end of the 2025-26 campaign, beating Bastia 2-0 away from home on the final day to pip St. Etienne to second place, Le Mans will have mixed feelings about their start to life in Ligue 1 this season.

Although they lost just one of their opening five Ligue 1 matches to start the campaign, Patrick Videira’s men have failed to claim a league victory in over two months, leaving them 15th in the table with eight points and only outside of the relegation places on goal difference.

Without a doubt, Les Manceaux’s weakness in the 2026-27 season has been their leaky defence, as Sunday’s visitors have conceded a concerning 19 league goals so far and are one of three sides alongside Lens and Strasbourg that are yet to keep a clean sheet.

Despite previously claiming victory at the Stade Velodrome, posting a famous 3-2 win in September 1994, Le Mans head into Sunday’s match in poor form, facing Marseille as massive underdogs, and knowing they’ll need to pull off another monumental triumph if they want to get their season back on track this weekend.

Marseille form (all competitions):.

Le Mans form (all competitions):.

Marseille are still without Italian full-back Emerson Palmieri, who is expected to return before the end of the year from a knee matter, while Canadian midfielder Derek Cornelius continues his struggles with a hip problem.

On a more positive note, Genesio will be glad that a cohort of key first team players including the likes of Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Nayef Aguerd and Geoffrey Kondogbia have all returned from the international break unscathed.

Netting an impressive seven Ligue 1 goals so far this season, including one in each of his previous three league outings, Amine Gouiri is undoubtedly Les Olympiens’ dangerman and will be hoping to close the gap to Paris FC’s Lassine Sinayoko at the top of the division’s scoring charts on Sunday evening.

Le Mans are certain to be missing Algerian midfielder Adil Bourabaa and former Everton defender Djibril Sidibe this weekend as the pair are ruled out with ankle and foot injuries respectively.

It remains to be seen whether either Samuel Yohou, who has reportedly sustained a head injury, or young French midfielder Martin Rossignol can fight off issues to feature at the Stade Velodrome too.

After signing from Ligue 2 side Guingamp in the summer, 32-year-old striker Louis Mafouta has been the visitors’ biggest attacking threat this season, scoring a respectable four goals in 10 league matches.

Marseille possible starting lineup:.

De Lange; Weah, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Garcia; Hojbjerg, Nnadi; Harit, Abdelli, Paixao; Gouiri.

Le Mans possible starting lineup:.

Kocik; Bamba, Torrente, Voyer; Vercruysse; Buades, Traore, Bretelle, Calodat; Mafouta, Gueye.

Having emphatically bounced back from their early season woes, Marseille will be confident that they can beat any opponent they come up against and continue their impressive rise up the table.

Although Le Mans will be desperate to turn around their poor form, we believe the hosts will be far too strong and are backing them to close the gap on the teams above by posting a convincing victory at the Stade Velodrome on Sunday evening.

#60638. What it's really like to kill a fellow athlete - and the terrible grief 'you carry for the rest of your life': The cursed band of haunted sportsmen reveal the nightmares that never leave them

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 19m • 📚 Deep Dive (3886 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

What it's really like to kill a fellow athlete - and the terrible grief 'you carry for the rest of your life': The cursed band of haunted sportsmen reveal the nightmares that never leave them

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 22:15 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • Towards the end of the Australian summer of 2014-15, as the country prepared to host the Cricket World Cup, I took a flight from Sydney to Hobart, Tasmania, to watch a Sheffield Shield game between Tasmania and New South Wales at the Bellerive Oval, a beautiful ground perched on the banks of the Derwent River.
  • Australian sport was still in shock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 22:15 EST, 19 November 2026.

Towards the end of the Australian summer of 2014-15, as the country prepared to host the Cricket World Cup, I took a flight from Sydney to Hobart, Tasmania, to watch a Sheffield Shield game between Tasmania and New South Wales at the Bellerive Oval, a beautiful ground perched on the banks of the Derwent River.

Australian sport was still in shock. A few months earlier, Australia's Test opener, Phillip Hughes, had died after he was struck on the side of his neck by a short ball from a young bowler called Sean Abbott in a game between Newly introduced South Wales and South Australia at the Sydney Cricket Ground.

Sources indicate that hughes was treated at the ground for 40 minutes and then taken by ambulance to St Vincent's Hospital in nearby Darlinghurst in a critical condition. 'Feeling for Phil Hughes after being hit,' former Australia Test cricketer Dean Jones wrote on Twitter. 'He is not in a good way! Stay strong Sean Abbott. Not your fault, young man.'.

Recent findings suggest that the impact of the ball had compressed a vein in Hughes' neck and when it split, it caused a catastrophic bleed on the brain. Hughes had emergency surgery and was placed in an induced coma. He never regained consciousness and passed away two days later.

Hughes was a popular, talented, gutsy cricketer with three Test centuries already under his belt. A small guy with the heart of a lion. He was 25 years old. Cricket mourned a terrible tragedy – some called it the sport's saddest day and the agony of Hughes' family was hard to bear. But there was something else. There was an awareness that two tragedies were playing out in front of us.

It has been revealed that hughes was lost but the man who had bowled the delivery that felled him had been left behind, desolate and distraught. Many thought Sean Abbott, who was 22, would never play cricket again. That he would not be able to find the strength. But that was why I had flown to Tasmania. Because Abbott had found the strength.

Phil Hughes was the golden boy of Australian cricket in 2014, with three Test centuries already to his name, when he was hit by a ball bowled by Sean Abbott and died.

Abbott visiting the Sydney hospital where Hughes was in a coma that he would never wake from, having suffered a catastrophic bleed on the brain.

That February afternoon at the Bellerive Oval, I sat among a smattering of spectators who watched Abbott walk to the top of his mark. His team-mates shouted encouragement to him. They were willing him on with everything they had and Abbott bowled his heart out.

'Beautifully bowled, Abbo,' one of the NSW fielders shouted after one ball to former Test opener Ed Cowan. 'That's a beauty, Seanie,' another yelled after the fifth ball of his first over, when Cowan jerked his head out of the way of a short delivery so fast he fell over. Only one wicket fell that afternoon. Abbott took it.

Sources indicate that it was one of the bravest sporting performances I have ever witnessed. Because even though cricket had voiced its support for Abbott, the sport could not protect him from his thoughts and from the knowledge he had become one of a cursed band of sportsmen who have unwittingly caused the death of an opponent during a contest.

Sometimes, tragedy in sport is not just the tragedy of the player who dies; it is the tragedy of the opponent who must live the nightmare of what he has done over and over again in his mind. To those that it has befallen, they say it is a grief that never leaves them.

That grief, that sense of a double tragedy, was brought sharply back into focus earlier this month when Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died in hospital the day after a sickening collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono. The accident happened in the final minutes of a game in Spain's Segunda Division, when Owono hurtled out of his goal and collided with De Miguel in the centre circle. He was shown a red card for the foul.

There was an outpouring of grief for De Miguel. I was among those who observed a minute's silence for him before the Barcelona-Aston Villa Champions League tie at the Nou Camp the next evening. Tributes continue to be paid to him. Owono, meanwhile, has become a pariah. It is mentioned that the 25-year-old rarely leaves his house.

Industry observers note that owono does not appear to have had the same sympathy extended to him that Abbott benefited from. His challenge on De Miguel, a striker who had had a peripatetic career in Spain's lower leagues, was reckless and cavalier. For him, the struggle with guilt and responsibility and public judgment is only just beginning.

FC Andorra will play their first home game since the tragedy against Leganes on Friday night but when they run out at the Encamp Stadium, a neat little ground beside a babbling river, the Valira d'Orient, and in the shadow of the mountains that make Andorra such a popular ski resort, Owono will not be there.

Earlier this month Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died in hospital the day after a sickening collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono.

Owono has become a pariah. It is mentioned that the 25-year-old rarely leaves his house.

The goalkeeper, who has 47 caps for Equatorial Guinea, was given the maximum sentence of a 12-match ban by the Spanish Football Federation.

Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera suggested Owono's ban 'might feel light' to all those mourning the striker, who was 30 years old, while FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique, the former Barcelona and Spain centre back, remarked the maximum sanction 'puts him (Owono) in a situation he does not deserve, because he is not to blame for all of this having happened'.

Recent findings suggest that no one knows whether Owono will feel able to return to football when his ban ends. Footage circulated of him in an on-field argument moments before the clash with De Miguel, and it was used to suggest that he was in an unstable state of mind.

Some have pressed for him to be charged with manslaughter. His Instagram account was deactivated after it was deluged with abuse, including messages which branded him 'a murderer'. It has been reported that his brother, who is also a footballer, has been the victim of abuse because of his association with Owono.

Recent findings suggest that owono has only communicated through a statement released by his club. 'These are the most difficult days of my life,' he wrote. 'I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to ​process what has happened. I feel enormous pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many questions to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.'.

I spoke to the great British fighter Barry McGuigan about Owono this week. McGuigan has suffered his share of tragedies. His brother, Dermot, took his own life. He lost his daughter, Danika, to cancer when she was just 33, in 2019. And in 1982, three years before he won the world featherweight title at Loftus Road, he nearly quit boxing altogether.

In a recent development, in the 12th fight of his professional career, McGuigan fought a Nigerian boxer called Young Ali at the World Sporting Club in Mayfair. He still remembers the clink of cutlery coming from the diners who were sitting ringside that night. That sound still takes him back.

According to recent reports, mcGuigan still remembers the sequence of punches that put Young Ali down in the sixth round of the fight. He saw his opponent's eyes roll back in his head and a feeling of dread washed over him. Young Ali, just 21, fell into a coma from which he never emerged and died five months later.

I spoke to the great British fighter Barry McGuigan (right) about Owono this week. McGuigan has suffered his share of tragedies.

'There was the horror of that and we sat and we waited and we prayed that he would be better and he never got better,' McGuigan told me. 'I didn't know whether I wanted to continue boxing. I thought: "If I can do this to somebody…"'.

It has been revealed that he shuddered when he talked about Owono. 'Other tragedies happen and other terrible things happen,' he noted. 'Life is a struggle. Something like that, you never leave it behind you.

'It is something invisible and it depends how emotionally vulnerable he is. He may never be the same again but I hope he is able to overcome it.'.

There are others out there in sport, still trying to overcome it. Think of Matt Petgrave, the Sheffield Steelers ice-hockey player who was arrested on suspicion of manslaughter after his skate fatally cut the neck of Nottingham Panthers' Adam Johnson in an Elite Ice Hockey League match at Sheffield Arena in October 2023.

Industry observers note that think of Jochen Mass, the Formula One driver, who spent years blaming himself for the death of Gilles Villeneuve during qualifying for the Belgian Grand Prix at Zolder in 1982, because he slowed and moved to the right in front of Villeneuve. The Ferrari ran into the back of Mass and flipped in grotesque cartwheels across the track.

Think of Matthias Behr, the German fencer who killed his opponent, Vladimir Smirnov, at the 1982 World Fencing Championships in Rome when Behr's foil blade broke during a match, penetrated the Ukrainian fencer's mask and pierced his eye.

Think of Gary Cully, the Irish fighter, who learned this week that his last opponent, Lee Reeves, had died after spending three months in a coma following their bout in Dublin in August.

It has been revealed that 'What a character and a gent,' Cully wrote in tribute to Reeves. 'It's never been nothing but love between us champ, can't really believe I'm writing this but RIP brother.'.

Nottingham Panthers' Adam Johnson died in October 2023 when opponent Matt Petgrave's skate cut his neck during a match.

Gary Cully (left), the Irish fighter, learned this week that his last opponent, Lee Reeves (right), had died after spending three months in a coma following their bout in Dublin in August.

Dr Victor Thompson, a prominent UK clinical sports psychologist, has studied the effect on competitors of being involved in the death of a rival.

'The biggest thing a player will have had to absorb normally is bad performance,' Dr Thompson says. 'Now he has to absorb the fact that he was involved in somebody dying. He will be trying to work out was it his fault? Is he to blame? And all of that, because the emotions are so high, gets associated with playing the sport in question.

'So when Sean Abbott thought about going out there again, when he thought about putting his pads on, or putting his kit on and being around team-mates or the smell of the cricket bat – it'll all be associated to that very traumatic day.'.

Recent findings suggest that university of North Carolina academic John M Silva III argued that aggression in sport is defined in two categories: hostile aggression and instrumental aggression. Hostile is when the main aim is to cause harm or injury to your opponent. Instrumental is aggression for a purpose, perhaps ball recovery or to sow doubt in an opponent’s mind.

Sources indicate that the interpretation of a player's actions at a time of high stress, frustration or adversarial combat is often central to the reaction to a sporting tragedy. Whether forgiveness is extended to or opprobrium visited on the competitor who has caused the death of another.

Industry observers note that that interpretation was used against Petgrave, who was notorious for having a bad disciplinary record on the ice. Some likened the action which fatally injured Johnson to a kung-fu kick and drew a link between it and some of his past behaviour. He was mercilessly trolled on social media. Team-mates, and many ice hockey fans, leapt to his defence and said any suggestion his action was deliberate was fanciful. They said his unusual action in lifting his left skate high was a direct result of being knocked off balance by a collision.

It has been revealed that petgrave could not return to ice hockey immediately even if he had wanted to. It was a full 18 months before the Crown Prosecution Service and South Yorkshire Police decided there was no realistic prospect of conviction for manslaughter and that no criminal charges should be brought against the 34-year-old Canadian.

In the intervening period, Petgrave's family set up a crowdfunding page, pointing out that he was unable to work or to return home until the CPS had decided whether to press charges. The page raised nearly £20,000 from well-wishers.

The interpretation of a player's actions at a time of high stress, frustration or adversarial combat is often central to the reaction to a sporting tragedy - as it was for Petgrave.

Petgrave did receive widespread support from inside his sport, with a standing ovation at his Sheffield side's next home match, while he was beginning 18 months under investigation.

According to recent reports, 'This has been the most painful and overwhelming period of our lives,' a message from Petgrave's family noted at the bottom of the page. 'Watching someone I love go through this has been incredibly difficult.

'Despite everything, we are doing our best to stay strong, and the support and kindness from so many people have been a source of strength. We continue to recognise the heartbreaking nature of this situation, and our thoughts remain with everyone affected. We hold on to hope that this will soon come to an end.'.

Industry observers note that petgrave now plies his trade in the minor league ECHL for the Indy Fuel, a team based in Fishers, Indiana. He is an ever-present this season, playing opponents like the Wheeling Nailers, the Greenville Swamp Rabbits, the Kalamazoo Wings and the Bloomington Bison.

According to recent reports, 'We understand the responsibility that comes with the great support we receive from this community,' Sean Hallett, CEO of Hallett Sports, which owns the Fuel, said when they hired Petgrave. 'We are confident he will be a positive addition to our team and our city.'.

I wrote to the Fuel, asking if there was any chance of speaking to Petgrave. They did not respond. The reticence is understandable and, in many ways, laudable. Players involved in this kind of tragedy are preoccupied with respect for the victims' families and the sensitivities that come with such terrible grief. There is nothing they can say or do to make it better.

Industry observers note that sometimes, it is the other way round. Sometimes, it is the family of a lost loved one who find a way to ease the pain of a sportsman eaten up by shame for inadvertently causing the death of a competitor.

Mass, who died last year, blamed himself for the sickening crash that killed the most exciting, charismatic, talented, electrifying driver in Formula One. As Villeneuve's Ferrari cartwheeled across the track, breaking into pieces, he was flung clear of the wreckage still strapped to his seat, catapulting across the track until he came to rest in the catch-fencing by the side of the circuit. He died of catastrophic injuries later that evening, aged 32.

In a recent development, mass was absolved of responsibility. It was a tragic accident. Villeneuve was running hot after a disagreement with his team-mate Didier Pironi and was pushing even his own boundaries. There were any number of extenuating circumstances but Mass still blamed himself. He retired from the sport the same season.

As Gilles Villeneuve's Ferrari cartwheeled across the track, breaking into pieces, he was flung clear of the wreckage still strapped to his seat, catapulting across the track.

Despite being absolved of responsibility, Jochen Mass (pictured in 2019) blamed himself for the accident and retired from the sport the same year.

According to recent reports, it was years later when he felt a tap on the shoulder as he was sitting on a plane. He looked up to see Villeneuve's son, Jacques, the 1997 F1 world champion, standing over him.

According to recent reports, 'I felt so guilty about what had happened and then suddenly, there was Jacques,' Mass recalled. 'He mentioned: "Jochen, our family – we never blamed you. It was a racing incident – just a wrong decision by the two of you."'.

In a recent development, all the shame that Mass felt ebbed away. He found his own peace just as Behr found redemption by sheltering the grandchildren of Smirnov and his widow, Emma, at his home in Germany to protect them from the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

According to recent reports, behr, tortured by guilt about the accident that killed Smirnov, had written to Emma 30 years ago but the letter was lost. When he did not receive a reply, he was convinced that Smirnov's widow blamed him for killing her husband.

According to recent reports, they finally met when a television documentary crew brought them together and Emma reassured Behr that she had never held him responsible. Behr has suffered from depression and suicidal thoughts because of flashbacks to the fatal accident.

Recent findings suggest that 'They are always there,' Behr remarked later. 'Even if I go into a liquor store and see vodka with the Smirnoff label on it, the thoughts of what happened immediately come back to me. But now that I am playing a part in the lives of Vladimir's grandchildren, it has come full circle for me. It was a gift for me. I can finally give something back.'.

Recent findings suggest that maybe Abbott has been trying to give something back all these years, too. Perhaps the fine career he has had is his tribute to Hughes. He has represented Australia in one-day and Twenty20 cricket and is the all-time leading wicket-taker in the Massive Bash League. He has represented Surrey in English cricket and was part of Australia's World Cup winning squad in 2023.

It has been revealed that many had worried that Abbott would not play again after Hughes' death. Not your fault, young man. Easy to say, harder to grasp amid the grief and the disbelief. But there was an outpouring of support for him, including from Hughes' family.

Perhaps the fine career 2023 World Cup winner Sean Abbott (bottom right) has had is his tribute to Hughes.

That afternoon at the Bellerive Oval, I asked him about the day's play as he came off. He mentioned he was happy with how it had gone. Afterwards, I sat in the stand with Abbott's team-mate Nathan Lyon, the Australia spinner, who spoke movingly about Hughes and about Abbott. At the end of the interview I thanked him for making the time to speak to me in such difficult circumstances. 'Too easy, mate,' he said.

Except it wasn't too easy. Inside, Lyon and the rest of Australian cricket were still in agony. Later that day, Lyon complained to Cricket Australia that he had not been expecting to be asked about Hughes. He was upset about my questions. I had made a misjudgment. Things were still too raw.

Lyon was comfortable talking about Abbott, though. 'The way Sean has carried himself through the whole incident, well, credit goes to him,' Lyon mentioned. 'He is a very impressive bloke. I've got a lot of time for him. He will do anything to help anyone out. He always puts mates first. He always has your back. He is a typical good mate. I'm proud to call him a mate.

'I think (Abbott not playing again) went through the minds of a few of us. But natural instinct will come over and you do what you do best and if that's play cricket, you go out and play cricket. It's about being around your mates and the mates who are there with him now, they're the guys who are going to get him through it.'.

Sources indicate that abbott has never spoken about the tragedy. He gave written evidence in January 2016 to the inquest into Hughes' death.

'I saw him start to sway and I ran to the other end of the pitch and I held the right side of his head with my left hand,' Abbott wrote. 'I remained on the field until Phillip was placed on the medicab and then returned to the changing room. Once in the changing room I felt confused and upset, I had a headache, people kept coming up to me but I cannot recall what they said.'.

It has been revealed that much of the inquest was dominated by suggestions that Hughes had been subjected to a barrage of short balls and sledging. The inquest heard that Abbott's bowling partner, Doug Bollinger, had remarked to Hughes 'I'm going to kill you' at one stage during the game. Bollinger denied that accusation. Abbott was exonerated of any responsibility for the tragedy that unfolded.

Only rarely are there glimpses of the impact that Hughes' death has had on him. At a tribute to Hughes on the tenth anniversary of his death, Abbott broke down and wept at the end of the minute's silence at the SCG. One of his team-mates put an arm around his shoulders to try to comfort him.

Abbott at Hughes' funeral in his hometown of Macksville, Australia, in 2014.

'The difficulty with boxing is that you are in this sport to hurt your opponent,' says McGuigan. 'Nobody believes - or wants to believe - that it is going to do lasting damage'.

McGuigan claims the pain never quite goes away. 'I had a love-hate relationship with boxing,' he says. 'The difficulty with boxing is that you are in this sport to hurt your opponent. Nobody believes – or wants to believe – that it is going to do lasting damage.

Sources indicate that 'After Young Ali died, I had to make a very serious decision about whether to carry on or not. I refocused and tried to make it a goal to win the world title and think about him when I achieved it. And the night I won the world title, I told Harry Carpenter through my tears that I was dedicating the fight to Young Ali.

According to recent reports, 'What happened in Tenerife looked like a terrible accident. Jesus de Miguel did not see him coming and he had no chance to brace for the impact. The outcome is the same as the outcome I had to deal with.

'I hope the goalkeeper will be able to come to terms with it. Sometimes, you can't. Sometimes, you are never quite the same, emotionally or mentally. It is the burden you carry for the rest of your life.'.

Aston Villa took a "big step forward" in their 0-0 draw with Sunderland, so says Unai Emery.

Villa drew a third straight Premier League match as they were frustrated by the Black Cats at Villa Park.

It is the first time Villa have drawn three straight Premier League games since 2014.

Villa attempted 700 passes in this match – their most on record (from 2003-04) in a single Premier League game, completing 624, their joint-most on record (also v Hull City in September this season).

They had 19 shots, but those chances were worth only 0.98 expected goals (xG) combined. Emery, though, was pleased with the levels demonstrated by his team on the occasion of his 150th Premier League game in charge of Villa.

Emery told Sky Sports: "A little bit frustrated, but how we are building our team and recovering our confidence in our style of playing, [this game] was a step forward.

"We were dominating, we were progressing with passes, and we were in a good position to control the game, but we didn't create many clear chances.

Industry observers note that "But this is the way and the idea we have to try and implement. We avoided the moment of them dominating us and avoided giving up chances to the opponent. We did a lot of good things.

According to recent reports, "It is not enough, but we know how we have to try and build the team and how we can feel better. One step forward, clear in the style. Keep going forward.".

Aston Villa 0-0 Sunderland Not sure we'll remember this game, will we.

Sunderland, meanwhile, have picked up more points in their last four Premier League games (five – W1 D2 L1) than they had in their first seven this season beforehand (four – W1 D1 L5).

Regis Le Bris' team moved up into 18th, though they will slip back down to 19th should Manchester United avoid defeat at Liverpool on Sunday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 21:13.

Roberto D'Aversa's Sassuolo tenure begins against Genoa on Sunday, with the Neroverdi in danger of slipping into the relegation zone.

The matchday 12 encounter pits two sides separated by four places in the Serie A table, with the higher-ranked Rossoblu chasing a fifth consecutive victory in this fixture.

Sassuolo's brief association with Alberto Aquilani lasted just 11 league matches, with the board in Reggio Emilia making another managerial change to arrest the club's poor run of results.

Admittedly, the Black and Greens made a respectable start under the former midfielder, collecting seven points from their opening four games as a three-match unbeaten run followed an opening-day 2-1 defeat at Atalanta BC.

However, mid-September's 2-1 reverse at Monza began a seven-match winless league sequence, and Sassuolo's defensive record under Aquilani made for grim reading.

The Neroverdi conceded a staggering 19 goals across five defeats, losing 4-2 to Frosinone, 2-0 to Como, 6-2 to Lazio, 4-2 to Fiorentina and 3-0 at Roma.

The defeat at the Olimpico proved the final straw for the 17th-placed outfit, who sit just one point clear of the relegation zone and two ahead of 19th-placed Venezia.

That underlines the scale of the task facing D'Aversa, who inherits a side that have conceded 29 Serie A goals, four more than both Monza and bottom-placed Udinese, two of the teams presently occupying the relegation places.

Daniele De Rossi's men will hope that the upcoming boss needs time to adapt to his surroundings as they seek to extend the Black and Greens' losing sequence.

The travelling supporters will welcome this weekend's trip, given that the Grifone have claimed four consecutive victories in this fixture, including two at Mapei Stadium.

Beyond those recent successes in Reggio Emilia, the Ligurian outfit enter this weekend as one of the competition's form teams.

Their 2-1 home defeat to AC Milan before the international break ended Genoa's three-match winning streak, during which they stunned Juventus 2-0 in front of their supporters.

Having collected 12 points from their last 18 in Serie A, losing to Roma and Milan during that improved run, De Rossi's men will back themselves to overcome any latest-manager bounce in Emilia-Romagna and claim consecutive away league victories for the first time since November-December 2024, when they beat Parma 1-0 and Udinese 2-0.

D'Aversa has several fitness concerns ahead of his first Sassuolo match: Cristian Volpato, Yeferson Paz, Daniel Boloca, Domenico Berardi and Vasilije Adzic will be assessed before Sunday's clash; however, Fedde Leysen (knee) and Ismael Kone (broken leg) are sidelined.

If three-goal Adzic cannot feature, the new manager will have to rely on Sebastiano Esposito and Armand Lauriente, who have scored twice apiece, to shoulder more of the Black and Greens' attacking burden.

Genoa, meanwhile, will look to Milutin Osmajic and Junior Messias to add to their respective Serie A tallies of four and two goals, while Stephan El Shaarawy has registered two assists in his last three appearances for the Ligurian outfit.

A relatively healthy squad further boosts the visitors' prospects, although Morten Frendrup remains doubtful due to the ankle problem that kept him out of the Rossoblu's defeat to Milan last time out.

Sassuolo possible starting lineup:.

Muric; Walukiewicz, Caleta-Car, Idzes, Doig; Thorstvedt, Matic, Sulemana; Dominguez, Lauriente; Esposito.

Genoa possible starting lineup:.

Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ehizibue, Wiafe, Traore, Ellertsson; Junior Messias, El Shaarawy; Osmajic.

Sassuolo's injury doubts complicate D'Aversa's first assignment, particularly with Berardi and Adzic potentially unavailable to bolster an attack already struggling to compensate for the team's defensive frailties.

Genoa arrive with fewer fitness concerns and a confident Osmajic, suggesting that De Rossi's men can secure a fifth successive victory over the Neroverdi.

York City manager Scott Lindsey “took encouragement” from his side’s goalless draw with Walsall.

The Minstermen could not make a breakthrough against the Saddlers, who sit just one point behind the North Yorkshire outfit in the League Two table.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It is not often York are kept at bay in the final third, but Lindsey did not read the riot act.

It has been revealed that he stated: “It was a really good game and as good as a 0-0 draw can be. We maybe deserved a bit more than a point, but there weren’t too many chances in the game.

“We had goalscorers all over the pitch by the end of the match and it’s not like us not to score, but we tried as hard as we could and I think the players carried out the game proposal really well on the ball.

“Alex (Hunt) had a massive chance in the first half, but there weren’t too many chances in the game and you have to give the opposition credit as well.

“I am still taking encouragement from the performance, as I believe whoever finishes above Walsall this season will be promoted and I’m also delighted with the way we defended.

“That’s our third clean sheet in a row (excluding the Jersey Mike’s Trophy) and we’ve put a lot of work into improving that side of our game.”.

Walsall boss Lee Grant applauded his 10-man team’s “great character” after they became the first league opponent to keep a clean sheet at York since Solihull Moors in September 2025.

The Saddlers held out for a 0-0 draw despite losing Courtney Clarke to injury in the 81st minute, having made all their permitted substitutions.

Grant said: “Going down to 10 men for the last 15 minutes, I’m proud of the great character we showed and it’s nice to be able to not concede a goal despite those circumstances at a place where so many teams have found that hard.

“There’s a reason why they have the ball more than anybody else in this division and score lots of goals and that’s because they have good technical players and are well coached.

“But, through the course of a season, there are so many parts of your game that you have to be able to demonstrate to continue performing well and I think we are showing all of those sides and I thought both teams defended their goals well.

“We maybe had enough of the game to warrant better chances than we created at times but, in the first half especially, we showed how we can control matches.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 21:38, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:43.

Kasimpasa will be looking to extend their unbeaten run when they welcome Alanyaspor to Recep Tayyip Erdogan Stadium on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts occupy fifth place in the Turkish Super Lig standings with 20 points from 11 matches, while the visitors sit 13th with 12 points and will be desperate to end a difficult run of results after losing their last four games.

Emre Belozoglu's sudden departure to Fenerbahce has not affected Kasimpasa, who have continued their encouraging run of form in recent weeks, putting together a five-match unbeaten streak in all competitions to move into contention for a place in the upper half of the Turkish Super Lig table.

The run began with a 4-1 home victory over Samsunspor, before they followed that result with a 1-0 away win against Eyupspor six days later.

They continued their progress with a 3-1 victory over Corluspor 1947 in the Turkish Cup, although their next league assignment proved considerably more challenging as they held Besiktas to a 2-2 draw at home.

Kasimpasa then produced another impressive performance in their most recent league outing, which was Alfred Schreuder's first game in charge, recording a 2-0 away victory over Gaziantep to make it three wins and a draw in their last four league matches.

The Apaches will therefore be confident of continuing their progress against Alanyaspor, particularly as they have yet to lose at home this season, although they have recorded just one victory, with the other four league games ending in draws.

The hosts will also draw encouragement from their recent record in this fixture, having avoided defeat in their last nine meetings with the visitors, winning seven and drawing two, including each of the last five encounters.

Alanyaspor, meanwhile, have endured a difficult period after making a reasonably encouraging start to the campaign, with their recent defeats leaving them in the bottom half of the standings.

Joao Pereira's side began their latest run of league fixtures with a goalless draw against Erzurumspor before suffering a 3-0 defeat away to Fenerbahce seven days later.

They subsequently lost 2-1 at home to Kocaelispor, with their defensive problems becoming more pronounced when they travelled to face Genclerbirligi, where they were beaten 5-0, suffering their heaviest defeat of the campaign.

Their struggles continued in their most recent league fixture, as they lost 2-0 at home to Trabzonspor, leaving them without a league goal in consecutive matches.

Their 4-1 Turkish Cup victory over 12 Bingolspor offered some encouragement between those league defeats, but the visitors have struggled to transfer that attacking performance into their domestic campaign.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 08:16 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

Premier League clubs have voted to protect the organisation's bigwigs from any individual legal action taken by Manchester City's sponsors.

Instead, the clubs - including City themselves - will foot any legal bills incurred by a potential corporate defamation suit.

Daily Mail Sport understands there was widespread support from clubs to insulate Premier League chief executive Richard Masters and the four other league directors.

The vote passed with 18 clubs in favour, and City and Nottingham Forest against.

It is understood Forest opted to vote that way as they felt they had not been given sufficient information or enough time to consider the proposal and its implications, as opposed to representing a show of support for City.

The matter was the first item on the agenda at the Premier League shareholders' meeting in the Savoy Hotel on Thursday and was addressed quickly with limited discussion.

Clubs had a paper for the proposed rule change before the meeting and there was significant support to extend the legal protection to individuals on the league's board.

This marks the first time since the Premier League’s inception that insurance arrangements for its board members have been reviewed.

Premier League clubs will foot the bill if Manchester City's sponsors sue for defamation.

In September, City were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules after a seven-year legal process.

An independent commission appointed by the Premier League found City inflated their revenues by £900million – disguising money from their Abu Dhabi ownership group as sponsorship revenue.

Etihad Airways, owned by the Abu Dhabi government, denied being ‘involved in improper commercial arrangements’ and said it was considering legal action in response to the verdict.

Meanwhile, another City sponsor, Etisalat - a telecommunications organization - is also weighing up legal action.

City, though, maintain their innocence and are appealing the decision, which could see them relegated from the top flight.

A snap 24-hour Tube strike that has shut one line and seriously disrupted another is set to affect passengers heading to events in the capital this weekend.

Members of the Transport Salaried Staffs’ Association (TSSA) working on the Piccadilly Line walked out at noon on Friday in a dispute over the dismissal of a colleague.

As a result the Piccadilly Line was closed and on Friday afternoon there was a part closure and severe delays on the District line.

TfL stated previously due to the shared infrastructure around the Ealing Common District line depot, there will be no service between Earl’s Court and either Richmond or Ealing Broadway from midday on Friday until Saturday evening, with a reduced service on the rest of the line.

TfL says services began to reduce after 10:30 on Friday and will not return to normal on the Piccadilly line until Saturday evening.

The Night Tube will not operate on the Piccadilly line through Friday night. The Night Tube service is expected to operate on Saturday night.

The Elizabeth line, DLR, London Overground, buses and trams are expected to operate as normal during the strike action.

However, these services are likely to be busier than usual as customers seek alternative routes, says TfL.

Customers travelling to and from Heathrow Airport, as well as those making journeys across central, west and north London, are advised to plan ahead and allow extra time for their journeys.

There are also a number of other planned closures on the Tube and Overground that will cause disruption.

There is a busy day of sport in the capital and disruption on public transport will affect the intends of fans heading to the games.

Lulu was at ex-husband John Frieda’s bedside when he died – on her birthday.

Idina Menzel turns heads in extravagant cape ahead of Royal Variety show.

Londoner charged after ‘knives and other weapons’ seized at busy station.

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events.

Chelsea’s home game against Leeds kicks off at 3pm, with the District line, a popular way of arriving at Stamford Bridge, still expected to be facing severe delays before and after the game.

While fans hoping to use the Piccadilly line as part of their journey to Tottenham Hotspur Stadium to watch the 3pm game between Spurs and against Ipswich Town at the will have to find alternatives, which is likely to make other forms of transport very busy.

District line delays could also hinder rugby fans wanting to use it as part of the journey to Twickenham to watch England vs the All Blacks at the Allianz Stadium.

Visitors to do any venues or destinations along the Piccadilly line may have to rethink how they are going to get to and from their destination.

The walkout will have affected anyone wanting to use the line to reach South Kensington to visit the Royal Albert Hall for the Royal Variety performance on Friday night.

Drake Millington plays the Eventim Apollo in Hammersmith on Friday night, normally easy to reach by Piccadilly or District line.

While others hoping to use the line for a night out in the West End, or visit for Christmas shopping or to see the Christmas lights on Saturday will have to rethink their journeys.

Visitors to Winter Wonderland in Hyde Park may also have to rethink their journeys.

On Saturday and Sunday there will be no service between Queen's Park and Harrow & Wealdstone on the Bakerloo line due to track work.

There will be no service between Euston and Watford Junction on the Lioness line on Saturday or Sunday.

No service between Euston and Watford Junction on the Mildmay line on Sunday, with also no service between Camden Road and Stratford after 10.15pm.

On the Weaver line on Sunday there will be no service oin the entire line until 10.15am.

There will be no service between Stratford International and Canning Town on the DLR on Saturday and Sunday.

On Sunday, there will be no service on the Elizabeth line between Paddington and Ealing Broadway until 07:45am due to Network Rail maintenance work. There will also be a reduced service between Paddington and Heathrow/Maidenhead.

Lee Stewart, Transport for London’s head of London Underground service control, said: “We are extremely disappointed that TSSA is proceeding with unjustified strike action in response to the dismissal of an employee working a second job while receiving full sick pay.

“We will do all we can to minimise disruption for our customers.

“I would encourage Piccadilly Line customers travelling on Friday and Saturday to check before they travel and consider alternative routes where possible.

“Our teams will be working hard to keep London moving and provide customers with the information they need to proposal their journeys.”.

TSSA general secretary Maryam Eslamdoust visited picket lines on Friday, and said: “Our members working in service control on the Piccadilly Line are determined to take industrial action in support of their colleague who has been unfairly treated by London Underground.

In a recent development, “We don’t take strike action lightly. Everyone here knows what it costs to lose a day’s pay.

“You’ve come out because you know that every London Underground worker deserves a fair hearing when a staffing matter arises.”.

The walkout is not related to plans for a series of strikes by Tube driver members of the Rail, Maritime and Transport union in a separate dispute over shift patterns.

Their first strike will affect the whole network on November 26 and 27.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The first 11 games of the Serie A season have produced some rather intriguing trends regarding AC Milan’s attacking productivity.

MilanNews recall how – after the important win in Genoa before the break – Ruben Amorim emphasised how this Milan team are still far from the final product he envisioned in the summer, especially in the final third.

The Rossoneri are improving in possession control and chance creation, but they often remain too far from the opponent’s penalty area for most of the game. This limitation has also affected Gonçalo Ramos, who has been forced to drop deeper, far away from the penalty box.

Sources indicate that after 11 league games, Milan are only 17th in Serie A for shots on goal, averaging 11.5 per game. Yet, they lead Serie A in average xG per shot, at 0.145. In other words, the Rossoneri do not shoot much, but when they do it is very dangerous.

This is also confirmed by the remarkable individual numbers. Adrien Rabiot has scored five goals from 12 shots, with a conversion rate of 41.7%. Diego Moreira is at 40%, Alphadjo Cisse at 38.5%, and Christian Pulisic at 36.4%.

The notable absentee from this ranking is the player expected to score the most: Gonçalo Ramos. The Portuguese has scored just three goals with 33 total shots and 5.35 xG, meaning a conversion rate of 9.1%. These numbers are far from those of his team-mates.

It has been revealed that amorim continues to defend him, emphasising that the problem lies primarily with the team being too deep. Milan must therefore start to generate more territorial dominance, to allow Ramos to operate closer to goal and for him to be on the end of what is clearly quality service being provided.

Manchester City goalscorer Elliot Anderson claims the club are "doing everything we can to fix" their defensive complications after they came from behind to draw with Fulham.

City had lost each of their last three games heading into the clash with Fulham and went behind in the 16th minute through Rodrigo Muniz's curler.

The hosts then had an Erling Haaland goal disallowed, but Anderson's first Premier League goal for City just before the hour secured all three points.

City are winless in four Premier League games (D1 L3) for the first time since January (D3 L1), while they have trailed at half-time in four consecutive matches in the competition for only the third time, after October 1995 and April 2006.

They have also conceded in nine consecutive games in all competitions for the first time since December 2019 (10), while they have conceded the opening goal in four straight Premier League outings for the first time since April 2012 (five).

Anderson acknowledged that City need to improve defensively, but he believes they are moving in the right direction.

It has been revealed that "It's very frustrating," Anderson told BBC Sport. "Going a goal down wasn't ideal, but it seems to be happening.

Industry observers note that "The second half was better, more intensity; we pushed higher. We just struggled to get the second goal. We're working on that [falling behind so much]. We are doing everything we can to fix it.

According to recent reports, "I was just playing a little bit higher up – focusing on doing the best job for the team. Fighting on the ball and off the ball.

Sources indicate that "That's my job on the edge of the box on corners from that side. Try to get a clean connection on target. Trying to stay calm in those situations and make good contact.

In a recent development, "Every game, we are learning things. We'll train harder. We'll be ready for the next one.".

The points are shared 1-1 @okx https://t.co/X3bxDu6v8o.

— Manchester City (@ManCity) November 21, 2026.

City almost got a quickfire equaliser, with Haaland hitting the back of the net just eight minutes after Muniz's opener.

However, Haaland's initial attempt was saved by Leno, who was then deemed to have the ball under control before the Norwegian followed in to bundle it over the line, and while Enzo Maresca did not say much when asked about the decision, he was not happy about it.

Industry observers note that "I think it's quite clear," he told BBC Sport. "But they decided something different.".

Fulham, meanwhile, are now unbeaten in their last five league games, drawing each of the last three by 1-1 scorelines.

They have now dropped 10 points from winning positions in the top-flight this season; only Brentford (11) have dropped more, but it was an impressive point for Fulham, who ended a 20-game losing streak against City in all competitions.

They defended resolutely against City's pressure, limiting them to just three shots on target out of 15 overall attempts, and Alvaro Arbeloa was impressed with the performance.

"I am happy with a point but would prefer three," he told BBC Sport. "I'm so happy with our performance – how we played and pressed them.

"We came here thinking we can beat them and not just defending. We could have scored one or two more. I'm so proud of the players.".

Industry observers note that "It wasn't easy [to persuade his players they could win against City]. After the international break, it's never easy, especially coming here.

According to recent reports, "I told them we lost the 20 games before; we're not playing those 20 games. If we believe we can beat them. If we fight for every ball and play with character and personality, we'll have the chance to beat them. They believed and played so well.".

Breaking: Virgil van Dijk delivers future patch amid Liverpool contract uncertainty

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (419 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Virgil van Dijk is unsure where he will be playing his football next season, with his Liverpool contract due to expire in the summer.
  • The Dutchman, 35, has plied his trade at Anfield since 2018 and is now a two-time Premier League champion.
  • He will be out of contract in June, though, and has revealed in a newly introduced interview with Sky Sports that it remains unclear whether he will extend his stay.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Virgil van Dijk is unsure where he will be playing his football next season, with his Liverpool contract due to expire in the summer.

The Dutchman, 35, has plied his trade at Anfield since 2018 and is now a two-time Premier League champion.

He will be out of contract in June, though, and has revealed in a newly introduced interview with Sky Sports that it remains unclear whether he will extend his stay. He is, however, clear that he expects to continue his playing career for several more years.

Per reports from BBC Sport, talks regarding a newly introduced deal are underway but an agreement is not close, and no resolution is expected before the new year. From January, Van Dijk will be free to sign pre-contract agreements with clubs outside England.

“The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion,” said Van Dijk.

“Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.

“At this moment of time, if anyone states that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either.”.

He continued, explaining that he will remain fully focused on on-pitch matters as he awaits clarity on his contract situation.

“But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game. Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the fresh year coming, we'll see then.

"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a significant part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.”.

It has been revealed that he added, matter-of-factly: “If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer.”.

#60606. A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 19m • 📚 Deep Dive (3870 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3870 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3. Electroceuticals targeting the autonomic nervous system have shown anti-inflammatory effects, yet existing systems lack the metabolic interoceptive feedback to fully restore immune–metabolic homeostasis4,5,6,7,8,9. Here we report an artificial neuroimmune axis (NeuroAxis) as a closed-loop immunomodulatory therapy for treating metabolic diseases. Analogous to its biological counterpart, NeuroAxis is solely powered by endogenous glucose, operating without batteries or wireless power transfer. It emulates the vagal reflex through closed-loop neuromodulation with metabolic interoceptive feedback. In a rat model of type 1 diabetes, NeuroAxis promotes the recovery of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells and reduces inflammatory immune responses; in a rat model of type 2 diabetes, it drives macrophage remodelling and reduces systemic chronic inflammation. In both models, NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation. Our artificial neuroimmune axis promotes substantial advances in treating metabolic disorders and represents a general approach for autonomously regulating interorgan communication, central to homeostasis and pathophysiology.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 21:40, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:42.

Konyaspor will be looking to halt their recent slide down the Turkish Super Lig standings when they welcome Besiktas to Medas Konya Buyuksehir Stadyumu on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts sit 15th in the table with eight points from 11 matches, only outside the bottom three on goal difference, while the Black Eagles occupy fifth place with 19 points from 10 games and will be hoping to maintain their push towards the top of the standings.

Konyaspor have endured a difficult run of results in recent weeks, winning just once in their last six league matches and struggling to find consistency in the final third.

Ilhan Palut's side began that sequence with consecutive goalless draws against Kasimpasa and Istanbul Basaksehir before suffering a 1-0 defeat away to Amed SK.

They then recorded a 2-0 home victory over Genclerbirligi, but that proved to be their only success during the period as they suffered consecutive defeats against Galatasaray (4-0) and Samsunspor (1-0).

Konyaspor were particularly disappointing in their defeat away to Samsunspor just before the break, failing to take anything from a match against a side sitting second-bottom and enduring a losing run.

The result further highlighted their struggles in front of goal, with the hosts having scored just six times in their opening 11 league matches, an average of fewer than one per game, while they have failed to find the net in seven of those fixtures.

Konyaspor have scored four of their six goals and collected seven of their eight points on home soil, although they were thrashed by Galatasaray in their last home game and now face a Besiktas side that have beaten them in their last two league meetings.

The hosts did manage to defeat the Black Eagles 1-0 in their most recent encounter, although that victory came in the Turkish Cup.

Besiktas, meanwhile, have enjoyed a more productive campaign, collecting seven wins, one draw and three defeats from their opening 11 league matches to remain within reach of the leading teams, sitting six points behind league leaders Galatasaray.

Vincenzo Italiano's side are also unbeaten in their last three league games, a sequence that began with a 2-0 home victory over Istanbul Basaksehir before they were held to a 2-2 draw by Kasimpasa.

Their subsequent European fixture saw them suffer a 3-2 defeat against Celtic, but they responded positively three days later by recording a convincing 3-0 home win over Genclerbirligi.

Dusan Vlahovic was particularly influential in that victory, scoring twice as the Black Eagles returned to winning ways in the Super Lig and demonstrated the attacking quality that has made them one of the more productive sides in the division, with only four teams scoring more than their 23 goals.

However, the visitors have struggled on the road, winning just one of their five away league matches and failing to win any of their last three, during which they have recorded one draw and two defeats.

Konyaspor will be without Adil Demirbag, who is recovering from a cruciate ligament injury and is expected to remain sidelined for the rest of the season.

Chidozie Awaziem is also unlikely to feature after sustaining a muscle injury, while Marko Jevtovic is working towards regaining full fitness and faces a late assessment.

Ugurcan Yazgili is another concern after picking up a hamstring problem, leaving Palut with defensive and midfield decisions to make.

Mostafa Mohamed, Diogo Goncalves and Ebrima Colley are among the attacking options available to the Konyaspor manager, although Enis Bardhi is expected to miss out through suspension.

Besiktas will be without Umit Akdag, who is recovering from a broken wrist, while Fabio Miretti is also expected to miss the match with a shoulder injury.

Emmanuel Agbadou is not expected to return until later in December as he continues his recovery from a knee problem, while Orkun Kokcu is also sidelined with a foot injury.

Konyaspor possible starting lineup:.

Gungordu; Andzouana, Baniya, Bosluk, Masuaku; Toth, Ibrahimoglu; Colley, Goncalves, Dompe; Mohamed.

Besiktas possible starting lineup:.

Nubel; Murillo, Taylan Bulut, Topcu, R Yilmaz; Ndidi; Trossard, S Ozcan, Olaitan, Fakili; Vlahovic.

Konyaspor have struggled to produce consistent attacking performances this season, and although Besiktas have been inconsistent on the road, their attacking quality should be enough to overcome the hosts' defensive resistance, with Italiano's side expected to secure a comfortable victory in Konya.

Roberto De Zerbi has revealed that James Maddison is still suffering from the same hip problem he sustained during pre-season.

The Tottenham midfielder has started just two games in all competitions this season and has not featured since coming off injured midway through Spurs’ 2-0 victory over Chelsea last month.

Maddison is available for selection against Ipswich this weekend and was also named in the matchday squad in each of Spurs’ last two league games against Crystal Palace and Leeds.

However, De Zerbi’s decision not to bring him off the bench against Palace or Leeds has raised concerns that Maddison is still not fully fit.

The 29-year-old returned from an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury at the end of last season, and he had hoped to use pre-season to build his way back to full fitness and force his way into De Zerbi’s starting lineup.

Maddison’s summer was, however, disrupted by setbacks, with a hip issue restricting his ability to train or play with the rest of the squad, and De Zerbi has now revealed that, four months into the season, the same problem is continuing to hamper the England playmaker.

“After Chelsea he had the same injury he felt in the Chelsea game and not a massive injury but he was not able to work. He had a problem with his hip,” De Zerbi noted in his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon.

“It’s not a major problem, but if you don’t work consistently, you lose the physical condition, and to play in this level of competition you have to stay in the top physical condition.

“He is still young, 29 years is not old, and he has to push and demand of himself the top in terms of physical condition, because if he is 80 or 90 per cent of his physical condition he makes the difference for us, he changes the games.”.

Maddison, who has been unable to train consistently this season, saw his professionalism called into question after Spurs’ defeat to Leeds earlier this month when pictures surfaced of him drinking with friends.

The incident in question occurred on the first of three days off for Spurs’ first-team squad, and De Zerbi indicates he has no challenges with Maddison’s conduct, instead joking that he was “very angry” that he was not invited.

“James is a top professional, top guy, top player. It is an honour for everyone at Tottenham to have players at this level like (Dejan) Kulusevski or (Micky) Van De Ven, (Jan Paul) Van Hecke.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 22:07.

Trabzonspor will look to extend their winning run in the league to seven games when they host bottom-placed Eyupspor at Papara Park on Sunday.

The Black Sea outfit sit second in the Turkish Super Lig standings with 25 points from 11 matches, three behind league leaders Galatasaray, while the visitors are 18th with just three points, five adrift of safety.

Thomas Reis has made an excellent start to his reign, winning all six of his league games in charge, with the latest victory coming in a 2-0 away triumph over Alanyaspor just before the international break, as Wagner Pina opened the scoring in the 17th minute before Muhammed Salah doubled their advantage in the 34th.

That result represented a strong response to their 1-0 defeat to Freiburg in the Conference League, which brought an end to their seven-game winning streak across all competitions.

Trabzonspor will now look to begin another run of victories, and their attacking and defensive records suggest they have every reason to be confident, having scored 26 goals, the fourth-highest tally in the division, while conceding just eight, the fewest in the league, as they build a strong foundation in their pursuit of a first league title since 2021-22.

The hosts have also won all five of their league games at home this season, and another victory would see them match the club's best start to a home league campaign, last achieved in 1984-85.

Meanwhile, Eyupspor are in deep trouble after suffering a 2-0 defeat to Kocaelispor last time out, their eighth consecutive league loss and the ninth time in 11 matches this season that they have failed to score in the division.

No other side has conceded more goals than Eyupspor this season, with their tally standing at 30, while they have also scored just three times, the fewest in the league.

Mustafa Dalci noted after the defeat to Kocaelispor that his side are entering a period in which they must start collecting points, but their prospects look bleak ahead of another difficult away fixture, particularly as they have conceded a league-high 19 goals on their travels.

Their head-to-head record against Trabzonspor offers little encouragement either, with Eyupspor yet to win any of their four previous meetings, drawing one and losing three, while they have failed to score in all four encounters.

Eyupspor Turkish Super Lig form:.

Reis has several absentees to contend with, including defender Chibuike Nwaiwu, who is suspended after accumulating yellow cards.

Batagov, Franculino Dju, Ruslan Malinovskyi and Okay Yokuslu are also expected to miss out, although a number of injured players have returned to training, with Ernest Muci, Tim Jabol-Folcarelli and Wagner Pina all potentially available after recovering from their respective problems.

Aral Simsir is also being assessed ahead of the match, while Cihan Canak and Onuralp Cevikkan remain injury concerns, leaving Reis with several selection decisions to make before naming his squad.

Eyupspor, meanwhile, have their own injury problems, with Talha Ulvan, Omer Ceyhan, Ahmed Abdullahi, Bilal Boutobba, Lenny Pintor and Simone Giordano all listed as unavailable or doubtful.

Dalci could therefore be forced to make changes, particularly in defence and attack, although the visitors are expected to retain much of the starting XI that faced Kocaelispor before the international break.

Trabzonspor possible starting lineup:.

Onana; Pina, Savic, Cenk Ozkacar, Cabral; Fabinho, Tufan; Salah, Muci, Saviolo; Onuachu.

Eyupspor possible starting lineup:.

Moldovan; Yavuz, El Yamiq, Jules, Yasar; Massanga, Akman; Michalak, Sabiri, Yao; Abdullahi.

Trabzonspor have the league's best defensive record, an impressive winning run, home advantage and a dominant head-to-head record against Eyupspor, all of which point towards a comfortable victory for the hosts, who should also be capable of keeping a clean sheet against the division's lowest-scoring side.

Ruben Amorim arrived and decided that he wished to keep the 18-year-old around, believing that he is ready to be the deputy to Goncalo Ramos, the fresh club-record signing. The Portuguese is struggling for goals, while Camarda is struggling for minutes, leading to suggestions of a new loan in January.

Oddo knows Camarda well having been the head coach of Milan Futuro during their first season in Serie C and then in Serie D following their relegation. Speaking to La Repubblica, he gave his take on the forward’s current situation.

“The talent hasn’t disappeared, but you have to be patient. I take Camarda as an example, one of the most promising centre-forwards I’ve ever seen,” he said (via Calciomercato.com).

Mikel Arteta gave a coy revision on Kai Havertz’s future at Arsenal, as he suggested a decision was not imminent.

The Gunners have moved to agree long-term deals with Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber and David Raya this month, while Piero Hincapie has been handed an extension as well.

The two obvious contract situations still to resolve are Martin Odegaard and Havertz.

Both are about to enter the final 18 months of their contracts, which run through to 2028, and it is understood that talks are yet to begin with either player.

Speaking on Friday, Arteta was glowing in his praise of Odegaard and made it clear that he "definitely" wants his captain to stay at Arsenal beyond the end of his current deal.

Asked if he felt the same way about Havertz, Arteta was less committal and indicated that there was no rush.

"With Kai, again, very, very happy with him, what he's doing, what he brings to the team," Arteta mentioned.

"In the right moment we will discuss these things. We haven't discussed all the things that are coming now for a while and suddenly they are coming.

"So in the background, the club ownership, Andrea [Berta] in particular, is very much into that and I leave it to him because I fully trust him.".

Rice has agreed a upcoming contract that will earn him a pay rise up to around £350,000-a-week, moving him into the bracket of Bukayo Saka as the club's best-paid players.

The midfielder's workload has again been a topic of conversation this season but Arteta emphasised that there was no need for concern.

"I think he’s in a really good place," Arteta stated.

"In the last game against Hull as well, we managed to take some minutes out of him. We're going to have to manage that to get the best version of him.

In a recent development, "But he's more than capable to do what he's doing, doing it again and doing it better. He needs to tell himself that as well because that’s the start of everything.".

Xabi Alonso has admitted he would like “more options” to pick from within his Chelsea squad, as he lamented their injury record and hinted at a possible need to strengthen in January.

The Blues’ boss has made 24 line-up changes in the Premier League this season, with only Tottenham (28) having made more.

That suggests Alonso’s team is unsettled, something backed up by their inconsistent result and which was put to the Spaniard on Friday.

“Once you have the whole menu, you can select what you like and I know what I like from the menu,” Alonso said.

“I would like to have more options with the whole squad available but that's something that's difficult to have during the season, but I am sure we will get close to that.”.

Alonso may well have been referring predominantly to players currently at the club while also alluding to the potential for his squad to be strengthened in the winter transfer window.

Chelsea are among the clubs keen on signing Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and are known to feel there is still progress they can make with their squad-building.

The Blues right now have Joao Pedro, Maxence Lacroix, Jorrel Hato and Reece James sidelined with injury, while Emi Martinez, Josh Acheampong and Jamie Gittens have just returned to fitness.

Alonso was asked whether he is concerned by the number of injuries his side of suffering, given that they are not involved in a European competition this season so fewer games ought to mean fewer injuries.

Recent findings suggest that “It is a concern,” Alonso said. “Sometimes you can analyse them and find a reason but sometimes it is difficult to find a reason.”.

Clarifying the timeframe on Friday, he said: “Hopefully before May. May is maybe late.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bayern Munich have opened the door to selling Jamal Musiala, or renegotiating his contract, amid concerns he may struggle to get back to his best form after being diagnosed with a fainting condition.

Musiala, 23, left the footballing world deeply concerned in August when he collapsed on-pitch twice in the span of just a few days, during pre-season friendlies against Heidenheim and RB Leipzig.

He later revealed in a statement that he had been diagnosed with a “neurological dysfunction”, adding: “(These episodes) are at the moment simply part of my everyday life. I am receiving the best possible medical care in this regard, and I am very optimistic... there is no additional health risk beyond this.”.

Musiala has since appeared in four league matches, three cup ties, and one Champions League match, tallying two goals and two assists in those appearances.

Bayern Munich’s decision-makers, though, are beginning to worry that Musiala, one of Bayern’s best-paid players, may not be able to replicate the form of his youth.

The club has opened the door to selling the former Chelsea youngster Musiala in upcoming transfer windows, though they acknowledge it may be hard to find a buyer given the player’s condition.

Industry observers note that speaking on Friday evening, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge told Sky Germany: “(Musiala) has a health-related issue. It's also well known that he has a contract involving very substantial sums of money. As a club, we have to consider how to deal with that situation. I think that's responsible and perfectly normal.

“What we know unfortunately suggests it will be difficult for him to get back to the level he has often shown here in this stadium.”.

It has been revealed that musiala earns a reported wage of €25m (£20.9m) per year. Until Harry Kane signed a lucrative latest contract in November, he was Bayern’s best-paid player, which Rummenigge fears may prove unsustainable.

Rummenigge continued: “[We need to] talk to the player, to the family and, above all, to the agency, because, with all due respect, those sums are then no longer feasible.”.

“I think we’ve handled the player’s situation very carefully, and we all want him to return, ideally in the best possible shape.
