Today's Serie A predictions include Napoli at home to Torino, as well as title-contending Roma travelling to Parma.

Having left for the international break on a rare low, Como will aim to resume their stellar start to the season when Cagliari visit Stadio Sinigaglia on Saturday.

Not only are the Lariani making a big impact in Europe, they have been breaking new ground in Serie A - but defeat to the champions recently slowed their charge towards the top four.

Free-flowing Como can score from all quarters, while Cagliari must head to the mainland on a run of three away defeats, in which they shipped 10 goals.

So, the hosts will resume winning ways after their setback in Milan, keeping them on the tails of Italy's top three.

Surprise Serie A leaders Lazio will welcome Lecce to Stadio Olimpico on Saturday afternoon, aiming to extend their advantage at the top.

Yet to taste defeat in the league, the Biancocelesti sit one point above reigning champions Inter Milan, while their visitors are hovering above the drop zone.

Though a fan boycott slightly negates Lazio's home advantage, they can comfortably claim a 10th league victory of the season.

Lecce's last success dates back to mid-October - against rock-bottom Udinese - and their wait for a win will go on.

Still unbeaten in Serie A this season, free-scoring Roma will return to action with a trip to lowly Parma on Saturday evening.

Sitting third - just behind reigning champions Inter Milan and city rivals Lazio - the Giallorossi averaged four goals per game as they posted three consecutive league wins before the break.

Roma can pick up where they left off before the break, as a limited Parma side will struggle to match their intensity and flair.

A fourth straight win in Serie A will warm the Giallorossi up for next week's tough trip to Paris Saint-Germain.

Separated by one place and one point, Napoli and Torino will return to Serie A duty on Saturday evening, when they meet at Stadio Maradona.

Both sides entered the international break on a grim run of form, sparking talk of another crisis for the hosts.

After two defeats and one draw from their last three games, both teams will be desperate for a win.

While Napoli are hampered by injuries and appear disunited, Torino have been leaking too many goals, so more frustration could be on the cards.

United head to Anfield to take on arch-rivals Liverpool in what will be Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge of the Red Devils.

The Argentine has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford, replacing Michael Carrick after a dismal start to the season for United, which has them sitting 18th in the league table after ten matches.

Harry Maguire’s late header saw United claim a famous 2-1 victory when the sides met on Merseyside last season, but Pochettino will need to summon an immediate turnaround from his side to give them a fighting chance this weekend.

But former Red Devils Neville still believes that United can get a positive, telling the Overlap: ‘I just don’t think the defence is good enough, the defence will concede goals, I don’t care who the manager is.

‘But I think it’ll be a draw. Probably.’.

Carragher, though, disagreed with Neville’s sentiment and instead backed his former side to prevail at home on Sunday.

Asked if United could get a draw at Anfield, he joked: ‘They can, of course they can. They won’t, but of course they can.’.

‘I think Liverpool will concede as well, but I’m going to go 3-1 [to Liverpool],’ Carragher responded when asked for his prediction.

He will make the decisions himself, and in the summer he chose Ruben Amorim as the head coach, working closely with him and listening closely to his transfer desires.

However, the intention to strengthen Milan’s sporting side has always been there, and Krösche has always been held in high regard by Cardinale.

Sources indicate that krösche officially stepped down from his role at Eintracht Frankfurt on October 18. This separation came after five and a half years of working together, with the highlight being winning the Europa League in 2021-22.

His best acquisitions were Randal Kolo Muani (bought for free after his time at Nantes and sold to PSG for €95m), Willian Pacho (bought for €13.65m from Antwerp and sold for €40m, also to PSG), and Omar Marmoush (bought for free after a year at Wolfsburg and sold to Manchester City for €70m).

Sources indicate that “Over the past few months, I’ve been intensely reflecting on my personal situation and my professional future,” Krösche said upon his departure. “I’ve come to the conclusion that I need a change. I also believe that a fresh impetus could be helpful to Eintracht.”.

The club recognised his great work: “Krösche has decisively shaped Eintracht Frankfurt. Winning the Europa League, participating in the Champions League, and the further growth of our team are testament to this extraordinary period.”.

Milan are his next chapter. Krösche will be responsible for transfer operations, likely taking the title of Head of Football. He will work closely with Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão, key figures who enjoy Cardinale’s trust.

Krösche will liaise with clubs around the world and with agents. He will have a lot of responsibility, but certainly not the final say, which will rest with Cardinale after the traditional consultation with the club’s internal working group.

Above all, it will be fascinating to see what Krösche will pursue and how he will balance the pursuit of high-potential young players (his strength in Germany and a long-standing objective for Milan) with the need for short- and medium-term results.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Bayern Munich have announced England captain Harry Kane will be out for a "few months" after he sustained an ankle injury in the 1-1 draw against FC Koln.
  • After netting in England's 3-2 win over Spain on Sunday, Kane returned to action for Bayern in Friday's Bundesliga meeting with Koln at the Allianz Arena.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 21 Nov 2026 00:27, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 02:37.

Bayern Munich have announced England captain Harry Kane will be out for a "few months" after he sustained an ankle injury in the 1-1 draw against FC Koln.

After netting in England's 3-2 win over Spain on Sunday, Kane returned to action for Bayern in Friday's Bundesliga meeting with Koln at the Allianz Arena.

Kane was named in the starting lineup as Vincent Kompany made his return to the touchline for the first time since he collapsed while watching Bayern's second team train.

As it proved, Bayern could not have got off to a worse start as Mikey Moore put Koln in front, shortly before Kane was forced off in the 20th minute.

The Ballon d'Or winner picked up the injury in the 15th minute when he attempted to reach Michael Olise's cross.

However, Koln full-back Joel Schmied slid in to win the ball while also making contact with Kane in the process.

The 33-year-old hobbled on for a few minutes before he eventually went to ground to receive treatment.

Unable to continue, Kane was replaced by Tom Bischof, who provided the assist for Nathaniel Brown to equalise with what proved to be the final goal of the game.

Bayern also lost Michael Olise to injury at the half-time interval, which compounded a disappointing evening for the reigning Bundesliga champions.

The Bavarians have since provided a swift but pessimistic revision on Kane's injury status.

Sources indicate that the statement read: "Harry Kane suffered a torn syndesmotic ligament in his left ankle during FC Bayern's Bundesliga home match against 1. FC Koln on Friday evening.

Sources indicate that "This was confirmed by an examination conducted by FC Bayern's medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be sidelined for the next few months.".

Bayern also revealed Olise will "receive treatment in the coming days" after sustaining a foot problem.

In line with Bayern's "few months" timeframe, Florian Plettenberg reports that Kane will be out for at least three months with the ankle problem.

However, there is an understandable caution in putting an exact timeframe on his recovery at this early stage.

Using the early three-month prediction as a guideline, Kane will miss Bayern's final four Champions League league phase matches against Lille, Slavia Prague, Manchester United and Real Betis.

Kane would also be a doubt to feature in the knockout phase playoffs if Bayern fail to secure a top-eight finish in the league phase.

In regard to the Bundesliga, he could miss the next 12 matchdays if he is out until at least February 20.

Meanwhile, England boss Thomas Tuchel will be nervously waiting to find out the exact timeframe for Kane's rehabilitation process.

If it is around three months, Kane would be back in time for England's UEFA Nations League quarter-final clash against Norway.

But if he needs longer to recover, England's greatest goalscorer would be in a race to prove his fitness in time for the two-legged clash.

The Three Lions will travel to Norway on March 27 before hosting the second leg a few days later.

The Red Devils captain was also dropped for a game after publicly criticising Carrick’s tactics following a heavy Champions League defeat to Como.

The arrival of Mauricio Pochettino represents a fresh start for Fernandes this season, but there remains uncertainty over his long-term future at the club given the 32-year-old is out of contract at the end of the season.

Fernandes has already turned down two contract offers from the club, and former Brighton striker Murray believes he could be eyeing up a move away from Old Trafford when the transfer window reopens in January.

‘I wouldn’t burst the bank [on a new contract] for him,’ Murray told Sky Sports. ‘I think he’s not the future of the football club.

‘Listen, he’s given his best years to Manchester United and unfortunately they haven’t won an awful lot, which he would have liked.

‘I think if he gets the option to move on, and it gets to January, and he can start speaking to other people, I think it will open his eyes up to see where he could go and if he could win things and finish off his career more enjoyably, because there have been years at Manchester United that have been really difficult.

‘He has been the standout player, but he is not the future and it could be time to part ways.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Marco Rose urged his Bournemouth side not to "think about records" after they recorded five straight Premier League wins for the first time in their history.

Evanilson and Justin Kluivert sealed the three points as Bournemouth overcame Nottingham Forest 2-0 at the Vitality Stadium.

Bournemouth's victory saw them move up to fourth in the Premier League table, before Liverpool, who are now fifth, face Manchester United on Sunday.

The Cherries are now unbeaten in all nine of their Premier League games against Forest (W5 D4), marking both the most number of times they have faced a side without losing and the most Forest have faced a side without winning in the competition.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Rose noted: "We don't think about records, we just think about the next game.

"We took the right approach. We knew it would be tough and we would have to stay patient, and that's what we did. It was a top performance and a deserved win.".

Rose was also impressed with in-form Evanilson, who scored in a sixth straight Premier League match, extending what was already the longest scoring streak by any Bournemouth player, or any Brazilian in the competition.

It has been revealed that "The way he works for us out of possession, works as a link player and goes deep. The way he scores is quite impressive," said Rose.

A sensational club record https://t.co/bcZNQ6y9kx.

Meanwhile, it was a day to forget for Oliver Glasner, who, on his 100th Premier League game, saw Forest muster a tame expected goals total (xG) of 2.07 from 18 shots.

Saturday's result also means Forest are now winless in their last seven away league games against Bournemouth (D2 L5), since a 2-1 victory in the 2014-15 Championship campaign.

"I think it's a deserved defeat. We have to blame ourselves for the first half. We made too many mistakes, especially when I see the two goals we conceded," said Glasner.

"The second half, we tried everything, so credit to the lads for everything, as they tried until the end. We got punished, that was more or less the result of this game.".

Xabi Alonso had been clear that he wanted his Chelsea team to match Leeds physically and mentally in the spirit of this historically feisty fixture.

What he got in the end, though, was yet more evidence that this young team are there for the taking by those who want to take the game to them.

Leeds were sharper and nastier in every aspect today, and while Chelsea took the lead through Emmanuel Emegha, it came as no surprise to see Daniel Farke’s men snap back to equalise before running away with the game with such ferocity that Alonso’s future will, for the first time, come under some scrutiny.

There were boos at the break with the score level, but Leeds firmly on top, and the shower of condemnation that followed the full-time whistle vocalised in the clearest terms that Alonso is under pressure.

Alonso’s Blues started the season ferociously and looked like they could challenge for major honours, but Chelsea supporters have been here before.

They were always going to need more than a few exhilarating attacking displays to nail their names to the mast of a title challenge, and so it has proved.

Dismal Chelsea well beaten by Leeds as scrutiny on Alonso grows.

Chelsea are nowhere near runaway leaders Arsenal, and they are once again looking over their shoulders at sides who are less well-resourced but more tactically defined and mentally resolute.

Leeds dominated both boxes and were first to every ball, bullying Chelsea’s defence just as Sunderland and Brian Brobbey had before the international break.

Industry observers note that lessons have not been learned from last week, from last season or, frankly, any point of the BlueCo ownership. Chelsea as a team, while not short on quality, remain short of leaders.

They have looked to shoehorn young men into positions of responsibility, and this is the inevitable result. Teams with nous, experience and bite will continue to see Stamford Bridge as a challenge they can scale.

This was Leeds’ first win in this corner of west London since the turn of the millennium, the latest in a long list of teams to head to a formerly impenetrable Stamford Bridge and make history.

According to recent reports, chelsea rarely have answers for teams who seek to raise the temperature of the game. When the game becomes stretched, Chelsea become increasingly erratic and tempestuous.

It is in these moments that the typically composed Alonso must do more to change the tide. His changes this afternoon came too late and made no difference. Leeds were in control of the game and the scoreline when Alonso turned to his bench just past the hour mark.

During his introductory press conference over the summer, Alonso was reluctant to say he believed he would get time to instil his ideas. His pessimism appears well placed because, just 11 games into the season, the pressure is ramping up.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin believes Chelsea’s players could not handle the ‘intensity’ during Leeds United’s 4-1 win at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

Chelsea took the lead in the first half through an excellent finish from Emmanuel Emegha but Xabi Alonso’s side were in front for just three minutes as Noah Okafor pulled Leeds level.

Leeds then came out flying in the second half and Leeds were given a penalty after Jayden Bogle’s thumping strike hit Rogers on the top of his arm.

Calvert-Lewin converted the spot-kick to put Leeds ahead and Daniel Farke’s side continued their dominance in the second half as Okafor netted his second of the game before Brenden Aaronson completed the deserved victory with a goal in injury time.

Chelsea have now been beaten in three out of their last four Premier League games, while only Coventry City, Ipswich Town and Crystal Palace have conceded more goals than Xabi Alonso’s side this season.

During his post-match interview with Sky Sports, Calvert-Lewin was asked what the message was from Farke during the half-time break with Chelsea already showing signs of fragility.

‘The message was just more of the same. I think we were going well, we just weren’t putting our chances away and we knew the next chance was coming and we’d have to take it,’ Calvert-Lewin replied.

‘To be honest, I expected Chelsea to come out with a bit more oomph in the second half but I think our intensity, the way that we played and the way we set up against them, they couldn’t handle it, and I think that reflected in the scoreline.’.

Asked what the message was ahead of the game against Chelsea, Calvert-Lewin replied: ‘Intensity, bring the intensity from the start.

Xabi Alonso has provided an update on Moises Caicedo after the midfielder was forced off in the first-half of Chelsea’s 4-1 defeat to Leeds United.

The Blues fell to a dismal defeat at home on Saturday afternoon with Leeds scoring three times in the second-half to seal a famous win in west London.

Caicedo started for the hosts having asked to come off at half-time playing for Ecuador on Tuesday against Bolivia, later explaining he ‘didn’t feel very well’.

During an aerial dual with James Justin in the first-half at Stamford Bridge, the midfielder suffered a heavy landing after twisting in mid-air.

While he was initially able to carry on, Caicedo went down again off the ball a few minutes later, covering his face with his shirt in disappointment.

According to recent reports, he was replaced after just 22 minutes with Jordan Henderson onto replace him. Caicedo did not go straight down the tunnel and instead watched the action from the bench with an ice pack.

Asked for an update after the game, Alonso explained the former Brighton star was in ‘pain’ and would require further assessment.

‘He has a knock and we need to wait until tomorrow to see how he is,’ Alonso said in his post-match press conference.

‘He was in pain and let’s see how bad it is.’.

Reece James meanwhile is also still absent as he recovers from minor knee surgery.

  • Ekitike has been on the sidelines since rupturing his Achilles in the second half of Liverpool's Champions League quarter-final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in April.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 21 Nov 2026 01:14, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 01:33.

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has revealed Hugo Ekitike is on track to make his long-awaited return to action in January.

Ekitike has been on the sidelines since rupturing his Achilles in the second half of Liverpool's Champions League quarter-final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in April.

The injury brought his season to a premature end and forced him to miss France's 2026 World Cup campaign.

Liverpool have continued to make do without Ekitike's services in the first few months of the season, and that is likely to remain the case for the remainder of 2026.

Having welcomed Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley back to team training this week, Iraola is hopeful Ekitike will make his return from a long-term injury absence in the fresh year.

"The strategy has always been January and that hasn't changed," Iraola told reporters ahead of Sunday's Premier League clash with Manchester United.

"If things go incredibly well, he can proposal earlier, which would be much better for everyone but right now, we still focus on January and that is the plan, yes.

"Hugo is behind [Leoni and Bradley], of course, and I think the target with Hugo has always been January.

"Even when we were naming the Champions League squad, I remember thinking if we could put him in or not. Everyone was saying that we think he can play the last two group games and that continues to be the target.

"He is behind Giovanni and Conor but if nothing is going wrong then January is what it should be, yes.".

Ekitike will miss Liverpool's next two Champions League league phase games against Club Brugge on November 25 and Porto on December 9.

However, he could feature in the club's final two matches of the league phase in the new year after being included in the Champions League squad that was submitted before the September deadline.

If he had been omitted, the 24-year-old would need to wait until the knockout stages for Liverpool to make an amendment to their squad.

But as it is, he will be eligible for the matchday seven meeting with Inter on January 19 if he can prove his fitness in time for the trip to Italy.

The Reds will then conclude the league phase with a home clash against Lens on January 27, just a few days after they face Man United at Old Trafford in the Premier League.

He has missed just one game through injury since joining the Gunners but his withdrawal at St James’ Park sparked huge concern for the champions.

Arsenal boast the strongest squad in the English top flight but former Premier League star Redknapp insists Raya is ‘irreplaceable’, warning Kepa is not of the required standard to come in and replace him.

Redknapp added any absence for Raya could prove extremely costly.

‘Arsenal’s squad, player for player, they have two players for every position,’ Redknapp told Sky Sports.

‘He will have an MRI assessment tomorrow, but at the moment I don’t know.’.

  • Gian Piero Gasperini believes there is no better striker in Serie A than Roma's Donyell Malen after he scored four goals in Saturday's 5-1 thrashing of Parma.
  • Roma ensured they remained within touching distance at the summit with a dominant display at the Stadio Ennio Tardini, with Rodrigo Mora also on target for the visitors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Gian Piero Gasperini believes there is no better striker in Serie A than Roma's Donyell Malen after he scored four goals in Saturday's 5-1 thrashing of Parma.

Roma ensured they remained within touching distance at the summit with a dominant display at the Stadio Ennio Tardini, with Rodrigo Mora also on target for the visitors.

Malen opened the scoring in the 39th minute after superbly controlling Emanuele Lulli's cross into the area before picking out the bottom-left corner with an emphatic finish.

But Parma hit back through Nesta Elphege within nine minutes of the restart, though three goals in the space of nine minutes later in the second half did the damage for Roma.

A 68th-minute strike from Malen was followed up by Mora's close-range finish, but there was still time for Roma's in-form striker to score and bring up his hat-trick, with the Netherlands international tucking home Wesley's inviting centre.

Malen added further gloss to the scoreline in the 90th minute, as Roma became the first team since the 1950-51 season to score more than 35 goals after 12 Serie A matches (36). In that campaign, Inter (38), Juventus (37) and AC Milan (38) all achieved the feat.

It has been revealed that and 12 of those have come from Malen this season. He is the second player to score at least four goals in a Serie A match for Roma in the last 40 years, after Vincenzo Montella on 10 March 2002 against Lazio.

Malen is also only the third player to score three or more goals in three different Serie A matches for Roma in the three-points-per-win era (since 1994-95), joining Abel Balbo (five) and Montella (five), leading Gasperini to lavish praise on his forward.

In a recent development, "Malen was already a strong striker in the Netherlands, Borussia Dortmund and Aston Villa. You don't play at that level without quality," Gasperini said.

"Perhaps I played him where he expresses himself in the best way. There are a lot of good strikers in Serie A, including young talents.

"And, of course, Lautaro Martinez, but right now Malen is extraordinary.

"He combines so well with our team, we perhaps get more out of Malen than we would do with a striker who is stronger on paper, but doesn’t fit as well with our style of football.".

— AS Roma English (@ASRomaEN) November 21, 2026.

Malen (26 in 2026) is only the second player in Roma history to score more than 25 goals in a single Serie A calendar year, after Pedro Manfredini (26 in 1960).

But, more importantly for Roma, they have now collected 30 points after 12 Serie A matches for the fourth time, following 2003-04 (30), 2013-14 (32) and 2017-18 (30).

Despite their thumping win, Roma remain two points behind Lazio after they beat Lecce 3-0 earlier on Saturday, with Tijjani Noslin starring with a brace at the Stadio Olimpico.

Lazio have won four consecutive home matches in Serie A for the first time since the period between September and November 2024 (five in that case under Marco Baroni).

However, Gasperini insisted his team must improve moving forward if they are to maintain their challenge with Gennaro Gattuso's side at the top of the table.

"We can always improve, both individually and as a team, but undoubtedly this side is growing," Gasperini noted.

"We conceded a bad goal at a tough moment of the match, but I saw a strong reaction from the team, and that shows the confidence is there.

"When we are faced with a negative or unlucky moment, we have the confidence to keep playing and get over it.".

According to recent reports, como also got themselves a win to move, albeit temporarily, into the top four. They beat Cagliari 2-0 thanks to strikes from Jacobo Ramon and Lucas da Cunha in either half.
